claim_text: KEPCO says an outside attacker broke into two of its systems and took data
summary: KEPCO announced on Nov 22 that it confirmed a leak of personal data from its KEPCO ON customer platform and its SRM procurement system, and said an external attacker accessed both systems and stole the data.
detail: Every outlet we read relays KEPCO's own statement; we did not read KEPCO's notice itself. In the Korean reports the company's wording is that the attacker is 'presumed' to have broken in and taken the data (Yonhap, Chosunbiz, Financial News). Outlets repeating one source count as one.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Five outlets report KEPCO's statement; none adds an independent check, and the company's own notice was not read.

claim_text: About 1.52 million people's data was leaked across the two systems
summary: KEPCO says 650,487 KEPCO ON users and 869,761 SRM users were affected, which adds up to 1,520,248.
detail: KEPCO has not published a de-duplicated count: Chosunbiz and Electronic Times both say people may appear in both systems. Yonhap (Korean) says KEPCO ON has about 9.2 million users, so the leak there is about 7.1% of them.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The figures are KEPCO's, relayed by several outlets; the true number of distinct people is not given.

claim_text: KEPCO ON customers: IDs, bank accounts, card numbers and billing records leaked
summary: Yonhap (Korean) lists 12 items from KEPCO ON, including names, resident registration numbers, phone numbers, addresses, bank account details, card numbers and billing records.
detail: The English Yonhap story names a shorter list: names, resident registration numbers, bank account details, credit card information, and electricity rates and billing records.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: KEPCO's list as relayed; the company's own notice was not read.

claim_text: Procurement system: names and IDs of company representatives, and staff contact details
summary: KEPCO says SRM exposed names, registration numbers, emails and company addresses of 426,827 company representatives, and names and work contact details of 442,934 KEPCO and company staff.
detail: Yonhap (Korean) says this is every SRM user, and that KEPCO is treating all of them as affected because it cannot pin down each person's exposure.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: KEPCO's breakdown as relayed by outlets.

claim_text: KEPCO learned of it on Nov 20, cut outside access and suspended the services
summary: KEPCO says it became aware on Friday Nov 20, blocked access from outside IP addresses, suspended the affected services, filed the legally required breach report and opened a desk for affected users.
detail: Yonhap (Korean) says KEPCO plans to ask police to investigate; Electronic Times says it already has. We could not settle that difference.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Steps described in KEPCO's statement as relayed by outlets.

claim_text: The National Intelligence Service and others are investigating the intrusion
summary: KEPCO says it is investigating the access route and attack method together with the National Intelligence Service, a cyber safety center at the climate and energy ministry, and outside experts.
detail: Yonhap (English) says the company will also share the breach details with government and financial authorities and ask them to step up monitoring.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Described in KEPCO's statement; no agency has published findings.

summary: KEPCO has not said how the attacker got in. Electronic Times reports the company said some convenience features became a target, with no detail. Its remark that attacks are getting more advanced is general, not a finding.
detail: The investigation is under way. We did not find a cause report.
label: Not established

summary: KEPCO and the outlets we read do not identify the attacker. We found no claim of responsibility in these sources.
detail: This page does not name or guess at an attacker.
label: Not established

claim_text: A separate KEPCO breach in October affected 35,528 people
summary: KEPCO said on Oct 1 that about 24,000 employees' data was exposed on an external webpage. By Oct 23 the count was 35,528, adding retirees and partner staff. Data was names, affiliations and phone numbers.
detail: Yonhap (Korean) and Aju Press report that KEPCO reported it to the privacy regulator and asked the Jeonnam provincial police to investigate. Both cite figures KEPCO gave a National Assembly committee member's office.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets relaying one set of company figures.

claim_text: Whether the Nov 22 breach is linked to the October one
summary: Yonhap (English) calls the October event a separate leak a month earlier. No source says whether the same attacker or the same weakness was involved.
detail: KEPCO says the cause is still being investigated.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing published links or separates the two incidents.

claim_text: No follow-on harm found so far, KEPCO says
summary: Electronic Times reports KEPCO said no secondary damage has been identified so far, and that it will ask the government and financial authorities to watch for abnormal transactions on exposed bank and card numbers.
detail: Yonhap (Korean) says KEPCO pledged remedies under the relevant laws if customers are harmed.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reports the no-damage statement; it is early.
